brief: Propose proof strategies for showing that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared in Lean 4, where each strategy teaches a different proof technique.
must: each strategy must be implementable in Mathlib-free core Lean 4
must name the tactic or term-mode construct it hinges on

brief: Propose ways to make Lean 4 proof search cheaper for goals about finite sets of natural numbers, without using an external SMT solver.
must: must be a tactic, a simp set, or a metaprogram
must say what class of goals it does not help

brief: Suggest ways to formalize 'a sorting algorithm is correct' so that stability, permutation and sortedness are all checked, each using a different specification style.
must: must be expressible as Lean 4 definitions
must be checkable on a real insertion sort

brief: Propose approaches to teach a language model to recover from a failed Lean tactic step, using only the error message and goal state.
must: must be trainable or promptable with fewer than 10,000 examples
must not need a human in the loop at inference time

brief: Propose new ways to approach the claim that every sufficiently large even number is a sum of two primes, framed as experiments one person could run in a week on a laptop.
must: must produce data or a counterexample search, not a proof
must not repeat plain brute-force verification

brief: Suggest unusual proof strategies for the irrationality of the square root of 2 that do not use parity or infinite descent.
must: each must be a complete outline in under 5 steps
each must name the key lemma

brief: Invent a puzzle that teaches the pigeonhole principle to people who have never seen a proof, with a surprising answer.
must: must be solvable on paper in 15 minutes
must not mention pigeons or boxes

brief: Propose ways to use graph theory to schedule a school timetable that make a hidden constraint visible instead of just solving it.
must: must name the graph and what its vertices and edges are
must give one measurable structural property to look at

brief: Invent a data structure for a text editor's undo history that supports branching undo and cheap memory use.
must: must give the operations and their complexity
must differ from a plain stack or a plain tree of snapshots

brief: Propose ways to find flaky tests automatically in a large monorepo without rerunning the suite many times.
must: must use only information a CI system already has
must say how it avoids false accusations

brief: Suggest approaches to make a command-line tool's error messages teach the user instead of just reporting failure.
must: must be implementable in a library of fewer than 500 lines
must not use a language model at runtime

brief: Propose algorithms for deduplicating near-identical log lines in a stream with bounded memory, each trading accuracy for something different.
must: must state the memory bound
must handle lines with variable numbers and ids

brief: Invent a way to make a hard-to-test concurrent program reproducible when it fails in production.
must: must work on a real language runtime
must not require recording every instruction

brief: Suggest new ways to review a pull request that catch what line-by-line reading misses.
must: must be done by a person in under 20 minutes
must not be a checklist

brief: Propose ways to represent a spreadsheet's formulas so that a bug in a far-away cell is easy to see.
must: must be a visual or structural representation, not an error list
must work for sheets with thousands of cells

brief: List unusual uses for a proof assistant that have nothing to do with proving theorems.
must: each must be something a real user could try this month
must not be about documentation or teaching
